newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Volvo Truck says Q1 E.Europe sales soar.
newsitem.headline: Volvo Truck says Q1 E.Europe sales soar.

text.p: Swedish vehicle maker AB Volvo's truck unit said on Wednesday its eastern Europe sales rose 77 percent in the first quarter to 1,065 units, making the company the largest foreign player in the region.
The company has a market share of 30 percent of imported cars in the region, Volvo Truck spokesman Stefan Lorentzson told Reuters.

"We increased our sales 77 percent to 1,065 trucks in the first quarter of the year and have noticed significant improvements (in sales) in, for example, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Poland and Russia," Lorentzson said.
"We are number one among the foreign actors on the market with a market share of 30 percent on imported trucks," he added.
The total market for imported trucks in eastern Europe has previously amounted to about 8,000 to 10,000 trucks, Lorentzson said, adding that Volvo has not made a forecast for 1997.
"We have said that we will be early on the growth markets and we have defined them as Asia and eastern Europe. In Russia alone we will add 25 service units this year," he said.
In eastern Europe there are 25,000 Volvo trucks and it is important to build up better coverage of service stations, he said.
The total market in eastern Europe is estimated at 60,000 trucks annually. The market is dominated by domestic players with a strong network of service stations, Lorentzson said.
